children: Shares of Bajaj Finance Ltd. will be reacting to their September quarter results on Wednesday, October 21. The results were reported after market closing hours on Monday, October 19.
Bajaj Finance's Net Interest Income grew by 23.6% from last year to ₹13,335 crore, while its net profit saw growth of 28.7% on a year-on-year basis to ₹6,367 crore.
Operating profit for the quarter stood at ₹10,699 crore, a growth of 23.2% on a year-on-year basis.
to 1.06% from 0.96% in the June quarter, while Net NPA stood at 0.42% from 0.39% sequentially.
The management has made additional macroeconomic provisions worth ₹337 crore during the second quarter.

During the earnings call, the Bajaj Finance management said that there has been an increase in stage 2 and stage 3 assets due to transitional gold loans, but despite that, the management does not see any significant impact to its credit costs.
Excluding additional provisions, reported credit cost at 1.56% from 1.32% last year. The management expects the credit costs for the second half of the financial year to remain near similar levels.
Bajaj Finance is also monitoring monsoon-related stress across 720 districts, and is selectively reducing its MFI and B2B exposure.
The company also recently announced a fund raise of up to ₹17,500 crore through a QIP and the issue of convertible warrants to its promoters.
With regards to Bajaj Housing Finance, the company said that there is no immediate stake sale planned as of now, as they want to allow more time for the shift towards prime and near-prime customers.
has also warned that the margin compression could worsen

in the second half of the financial year due to the repo rate hike by the Reserve Bank of India and could exceed the 10-15 basis points guided for earlier, after a five basis points compression already seen in the first half.

On the positive side, the management has raised its full-year AUM growth guidance to 26% to 27% from 22% to 24% earlier, while reiterating its medium-term AUM growth guidance of 23% to 25%. The management has also reiterated its
target of reaching ₹11 lakh crore in Assets Under Management by financial year 2030.
Shares of Bajaj Finance ended 1.4% lower on Monday at ₹957.35 ahead of the results announcement. The stock has again turned negative on a year-to-date basis.

title: Bajaj Finance shares in focus after Q2 results, increased AUM guidance, margin pressure
